intro: Calculate your Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) and Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) to find the right calorie target for weight loss, maintenance or muscle gain.

result.deficit: For weight loss we suggest a 500 kcal/day deficit.
result.surplus: For muscle gain we suggest a 300 kcal/day surplus.

formula.title: Mifflin-St Jeor Formula
formula.explanation: We use the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, considered the most accurate for most adults. TDEE = BMR × Activity Multiplier.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.a1: Basal Metabolic Rate is the number of calories your body burns at complete rest to maintain vital functions like breathing, circulation and cell repair.
faq.a2: Total Daily Energy Expenditure is your BMR multiplied by an activity factor. It represents the total calories you burn in a day including exercise.
faq.a3: The Mifflin-St Jeor equation is within ±10% for most people. Individual metabolic rates vary due to genetics, hormones and muscle mass.
faq.q4: How many calories should I eat to lose weight?
faq.a4: A deficit of 500 kcal/day typically leads to approximately 0.5 kg of fat loss per week. Avoid going below 1200 kcal/day (women) or 1500 kcal/day (men) without medical supervision.
faq.q5: Should I eat back exercise calories?
faq.a5: If you use the TDEE method, your exercise is already accounted for. If you use BMR as your base and log workouts separately, you may eat back a portion of those calories.
